name: Digital Forensics & Incident Response
tagline: Analyze memory, disk, carved files, artifacts, and timelines from your own systems, lab evidence, and incident-response cases you legally possess.

tools.name: dd
tools.desc: GNU coreutils bit-copy utility that creates a byte-for-byte image of any block device — the universal imaging baseline every forensics distro ships.
tools.when: Quick raw image of your own drive, USB stick, or SD card when you just need a faithful copy and will hash it yourself.

tools.name: ddrescue
tools.desc: GNU data-recovery imager that resists read errors, logs bad blocks, and retries them after the rest of the media is copied — built to salvage failing or damaged storage.
tools.when: The drive clicks or returns I/O errors: let ddrescue build a mostly-complete image first, then analyze the rescued copy instead of the failing disk.

tools.name: dc3dd
tools.desc: Forensic fork of GNU dd that adds on-the-fly hashing, split output, pattern wiping, and a detailed acquisition log — evidence-grade imaging in one pass.
tools.when: Capture a definitive, hash-verified image of a source drive before analysis so you examine the copy, not the live evidence.

tools.name: FTK Imager
tools.desc: Exterro's free, widely-used acquisition and preview tool: images drives/memory to raw, E01, and AFF formats, computes hashes, and mounts images for instant browsing.
tools.when: Click-driven imaging with E01 support (or compressed raw) straight to a case folder; it also does live RAM acquisition when needed.
tools.install: Download the free installer from exterro.com and run FTK Imager

tools.name: Guymager
tools.desc: Linux GUI forensic imager producing flat (dd), EWF (E01), and AFF images with multi-threaded pipelined reads and verification progress per device.
tools.when: Window-based imaging with progress bars and check-verification on a Linux analysis box when you prefer a GUI over dc3dd's command line.

tools.name: forensicsiso
tools.desc: Full DFIR workstation — disk/memory/log/pcap/registry/browser/email parsing, super-timelining, cross-artifact correlation, chain-of-custody.
tools.when: Running end-to-end incident-response analysis on acquired evidence.

tools.name: KAPE
tools.desc: Kroll Artifact Parser and Extractor: selects forensically useful artifacts (registry hives, EVTX, Prefetch, MFT, browser files) from a live device or mounted image, then parses them with bundled tools in minutes.
tools.when: Speed triage in your own incident response or lab: point it at a live Windows box or mounted image and get parsed artifacts quickly; extend with community KapeFiles targets.
tools.install: Download KAPE from Kroll's site (or GitHub releases) and run kape.exe

tools.name: Magnet RAM Capture
tools.desc: Free Windows memory acquisition tool that dumps physical RAM to raw .DMP files with a small footprint and optional command-line mode — ideal for preserving volatile evidence before it disappears.
tools.when: Grab the memory of a live lab or incident host before anything else — the .DMP output feeds straight into Volatility.
tools.install: Fill the download form at magnetforensics.com and run the standalone capture utility

tools.name: The Sleuth Kit
tools.desc: Command-line suite for raw/EWF images: mmls for partition layout, fls/icat to list and extract inodes, istat for metadata, and tsk_recover for recovery — the engine underneath Autopsy.
tools.when: Scripted or headless analysis, or when you need precise inode-level answers Autopsy hides behind its GUI.

tools.name: Autopsy
tools.desc: GUI platform built on The Sleuth Kit: opens images and live drives, recovers deleted files, and runs ingest modules for web history, keyword search, and carving inside a case workflow.
tools.when: First-pass interactive examination of a drive or memory-card image from your own casework or lab — ingest everything, then drill into findings.
tools.install: Download the installer from sleuthkit.org/autopsy and run it

tools.name: foremost
tools.desc: AFOSI-origin header/footer and data-structure carver that extracts JPEG, ZIP, PDF, and other signatures from raw images or drives via a configurable file-type table.
tools.when: Unallocated-space fishing: run it on an image or free-space carve to recover deleted files the live filesystem no longer lists.

tools.name: scalpel
tools.desc: Filesystem-independent carver using a header/footer definition database — a rewrite of foremost's engine with per-type carve-size tuning; the original repo is stale, machn1k/scalpel-2.0 carries it on.
tools.when: Stubborn image carries where you need tuned per-type size limits or a second carving engine beyond foremost defaults.

tools.name: TestDisk / PhotoRec
tools.desc: Signature-based recovery of 440+ file formats plus TestDisk for partition-table repair and undelete; no filename reconstruction, but deep salvage on corrupted or reformatted media.
tools.when: Last-ditch recovery from a reformatted or damaged partition or thumb drive in your own hardware lab.

tools.name: bulk_extractor
tools.desc: Scans any input byte-by-byte and extracts emails, URLs, credit-card numbers, JPEGs, and JSON to feature files — recursively decoding compressed or encoded blocks without parsing the filesystem.
tools.when: Rapid 'what is in this blob' extraction over images or wiped drives before deep filesystem analysis.

tools.name: Volatility 3
tools.desc: The de-facto memory forensics framework: plugin-based analysis of RAM dumps (raw, EWF, crash/hibernation) across Windows, Linux, macOS, and Android — processes, network artifacts, injected code, and more.
tools.when: Start here with any memory dump from a lab box or captured incident host; run pslist/pscan, netscan, and malfind to build the runtime picture.

tools.name: Volatility 2
tools.desc: The classic Python 2 framework (archived but stable) with the deepest plugin ecosystem and profile-based analysis for older Windows, Linux, and macOS dumps.
tools.when: Reach for it when a legacy or niche image lacks a Volatility 3 symbol table, or a plugin you need only exists in the classic tree.

tools.name: Rekall
tools.desc: Google-origin memory forensics framework born from Volatility during the 2.x era — effectively dormant since ~2020 with legacy artifacts in gray matter for older Windows/Linux images.
tools.when: Reading old IR research or cross-checking a niche plugin result on a vintage dump; expect to maintain it yourself.

tools.name: MemProcFS
tools.desc: Mounts a memory dump or live target (PCILeech FPGA/LeechAgent) as a virtual filesystem of processes, registry, and artifacts, with a batch forensic mode and YARA scanning.
tools.when: Fast interactive triage of a Windows dump without plugin CLI gymnastics, or live acquisition during your own incident response.

tools.name: Redline
tools.desc: Mandiant's free endpoint and memory investigation GUI: collects a volatile data set (processes, network, services, registry) from a live host or a memory dump and flags suspicious items with ATT&CK mapping — slower-moving now but still used in FTK/IR workflows.
tools.when: Point-and-click triage of a live Windows endpoint or captured memory when the CLI frameworks feel heavy for your own casework.
tools.install: Download Redline from Mandiant's free-tools page and let the wizard collect or open a memory image

tools.name: strings
tools.desc: GNU binutils classic that extracts printable ASCII/Unicode sequences from a raw memory dump — still the fastest way to spot C2 URLs, commands, and keys before the framework work.
tools.when: Instant grep-ish pass over a dump for notable indicators, or targeted hunting using the output piped into a socket/crypto-constant search.
tools.install: sudo apt install binutils && strings <dump> | grep -E '[0-9]+\.'

tools.name: Eric Zimmerman's Tools
tools.desc: Suite of focused parsers — RECmd/Registry Explorer, PECmd (Prefetch), LECmd (LNK), JLECmd (JumpLists), ShellBags, Amcache, MFTECmd — answering execution-timeline questions from individual artifacts.
tools.when: Deep-dive a targeted artifact set: ask 'what executed, when, by whom' via Prefetch, LNK/JumpList, Amcache, and registry traces.

tools.name: EvtxECmd
tools.desc: Eric Zimmerman's direct EVTX event-log parser turning .evtx databases into CSV/JSON with formatted timestamps and named fields, ready for Timeline Explorer.
tools.when: Convert raw Windows event logs from a mounted image or collection set into a queryable CSV before building your timeline.
tools.install: Download from EricZimmerman GitHub releases (part of Get-ZimmermanTools)

tools.name: Hayabusa
tools.desc: Yamato Security's Rust-based Windows event-log fast forensics tool that applies a huge Mitre-Attack-mapped sigma-rule library to EVTX dumps and outputs alert timelines in seconds.
tools.when: Hunt lateral movement, logon anomalies, and persistence across a full C:\Windows\System32\winevt\Logs collection or exported .evtx set.
tools.install: Download the release binary for your OS and run hayabusa csv-timeline -d <evtx_dir>

tools.name: APT-Hunter
tools.desc: Python-based EVTX analysis tool feeding exported Windows event logs through threat-hunting queries to detect hacking activity and TTPs via suspicious event correlations.
tools.when: Point it at your exported .evtx logs for a quick attacker-TTP posture check before going deep with sigma/hunting frameworks.

tools.name: plaso / log2timeline
tools.desc: log2timeline extracts timestamped events (filesystem, registry, EVTX, browser, application logs) from an image or mount point into a Plaso storage file; psort turns it into a filtered super-timeline.
tools.when: Build the master super-timeline of an image: collect once with log2timeline, then slice and filter per question with psort.

tools.name: Timeline Explorer
tools.desc: Eric Zimmerman's high-performance CSV timeline viewer with filters, bookmarks, and quick histogramning — the companion screen for Plaso/EvtxECmd CSV output.
tools.when: Load a super-timeline or artifact CSV and filter/hide columns interactively to answer 'what happened when' without SQL.
tools.install: Download from ericzimmerman.github.io (Chocolatey: choco install timelineexplorer)

tools.name: Hindsight
tools.desc: Obsidian Forensics' Chromium/Chrome/Edge history parser: decrypts login data, decodes History/SQLite, typed URLs, cookies, and downloads into a readable report with timestamp decoding.
tools.when: Extract reconstructable browser activity from the Chrome/Edge profile directory of a mounted image or live host in your own case.

tools.name: DB Browser for SQLite
tools.desc: Full-featured GUI for reading and querying SQLite databases — the manual backstop when you need to poke raw browser History/places.sqlite rows yourself.
tools.when: Directly inspect a browser database (history, cookies, bookmarks, cache index) when a parser misses a field or you want ad-hoc SQL.

tools.name: BrowserHistoryViewer
tools.desc: Foxton Forensics' free viewer for Chrome, Edge, Firefox, IE, and Safari history with keyword/date filtering, timezone-aware timestamps, and easy CSV export.
tools.when: Quick, clean table of browsing history with proper timestamp conversion for a report or super-timeline merge.
tools.install: Download the free installer from foxtonforensics.com

tools.name: BrowsingHistoryView
tools.desc: NirSoft utility that reads history from all major browsers (Firefox, Chrome, IE/Edge, Opera) into one table across all user profiles, local or from an external drive.
tools.when: One-pass aggregation of every browser profile's history on a live system or mounted image into a single viewable export.
tools.install: Download BrowsingHistoryView.zip from nirsoft.net and run the executable

tools.name: ChromeHistoryView
tools.desc: NirSoft tool focused purely on Chrome/Chromium-based history: reads the local History database and dumps entries to CSV/HTML with optional read from the live profile.
tools.when: Chrome-only deep dive when you want granular control and export options Eclipse the general aggregators.

tools.name: ChromeCacheView
tools.desc: NirSoft Chrome cache reader that lists files stored in the Cache/Cache_Data folders with URLs, sizes, and download times, plus option to copy recoverable cached files to a folder.
tools.when: Recover cached images/videos being staged by a live chrome user, or enumerate what content was browsed even after history deletion.
